scholarships.title: GIST Government-sponsored Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology (GIST)

existing.description: GIST states that tuition is 'fully supported: 3,607,000 won per semester' for all students and lists monthly stipends for all international students: a student allowance of 140,000 won per month for M.S. and 295,000 won per month for Ph.D. students, a meal allowance of nearly 100,000 won per month and an international student allowance of 120,000 won per month. The Government-sponsored Scholarship page sets the master's scholarship allowance at 140,000 won per month for a maximum of four enrolled semesters and the doctoral teaching-assistant benefit at 295,000 won per month for a maximum of eight. GIST also supports 60% of National Health Insurance and reimburses one-way airfare to Korea for incoming international students, and there is no separate scholarship application. The 2027 Spring admission application period runs from 7 September to 7 October 2026 (KST).
eligibility: Enrolled as a GIST student (admission to GIST is the qualifying event)
Government scholarship student for the master's scholarship allowance (maximum 4 enrolled semesters)
Government scholarship student for the doctoral teaching-assistant benefit (maximum 8 enrolled semesters)
International student for the international student allowance of 120,000 won per month
At least 9 credits earned in the previous semester for the student and meal allowances
GPA of 3.0 or higher (out of 4.5) in the previous semester for the international student allowance
existing.eligibility_summary: All students enrolled at GIST receive full tuition support, and all international students receive the monthly stipends, health insurance support and one-way flight reimbursement; the government-sponsored scholarship allowance applies to government scholarship students (master's up to 4 semesters, doctoral up to 8). Eligibility is tied to admission to GIST rather than to a separate scholarship application.

The scholarship itself needs no separate application - it is granted to admitted students.

scholarships.title: DGIST Government Scholarship for International Graduate Students
scholarships.official_source: DGIST (Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology)

existing.description: DGIST's international graduate admissions site publishes a Graduate Scholarship page describing two scholarship tracks for admitted international graduate students. The Government Scholarship track, described as scholarship benefits funded by the Korean government, provides full tuition coverage plus an annual stipend of at least KRW 9.6 million for Master's students and at least KRW 14.04 million for PhD students, with additional incentives varying by research performance, and is open to DGIST's science and engineering departments. DGIST states that admission to the graduate school guarantees automatic registration to the scholarship without any additional process, so the award follows admission rather than a separate scholarship application. The next published admission window is the 2027 Spring 3rd round, whose online application period runs 5-19 November 2026.
eligibility: Must be an international (non-Korean) applicant admitted to a DGIST graduate programme

Department must be one of those listed for the scholarship: Physics and Chemistry; Electrical Engineering and Computer Science; Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering; Energy Science and Engineering; Brain Sciences; New Biology; Artificial Intelligence Major in Interdisciplinary Studies; Artificial Intelligence; Biomedical Science & Engineering; Quantum Information Science
Must apply to only one department (or programme) for each intake
DGIST states that admission to the graduate school guarantees automatic registration to the scholarship, so no separate scholarship application is required
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to international applicants who are admitted to a DGIST graduate programme in one of DGIST's listed departments. DGIST states that admission to the graduate school guarantees automatic registration to the scholarship without any additional process.
benefits: Full tuition coverage for the degree programme
Master's stipend of at least KRW 9.6 million per year, plus additional incentives that vary with research performance
PhD stipend of at least KRW 14.04 million per year, plus additional incentives that vary with research performance
On-campus housing in Biseul Village: single room KRW 220,000 per month, double room KRW 170,000 per month, married student apartment KRW 290,000 per month (prices subject to change by academic year)
coverage: Full tuition coverage (tuition fees vary by department and major, so DGIST asks applicants to confirm with the department)
Annual stipend of at least KRW 9,600,000 for the Master's program plus additional incentives
Annual stipend of at least KRW 14,040,000 for the PhD program plus additional incentives
Access to on-campus housing in Biseul Village at published rates
requirements: Apply online through DGIST's UwayApply system during a published admission round
Complete the application form and upload admission documents
Pass document screening and the online interview
documents: Admission documents uploaded through UwayApply (DGIST publishes the detailed list in its admission brochure and the 2027 Spring Admission brochure download on the Application page)
application_method: Sign up and log in to UwayApply
Fill out the online application form for the chosen department
Await document screening results and take part in the online interview
existing.selection_notes: DGIST states that admission to the graduate school guarantees automatic registration to the scholarship without any additional process. The amount of additional incentives on top of the minimum annual stipend varies depending on research performance. For the DGIST-funded track, DGIST instead asks applicants to check with the department or prospective academic supervisor about eligibility.
existing.best_fit: International applicants to DGIST's science, engineering and interdisciplinary STEM graduate programmes (physics and chemistry, electrical engineering and computer science, robotics and mechatronics, energy science, brain sciences, new biology, artificial intelligence, biomedical science and engineering, quantum information science).
existing.notes: DGIST publishes a separate DGIST Scholarship track funded by DGIST funds, external donations or research grants, limited to certain departments, which requires tuition payment with an additional stipend equal to the tuition fee (Master's at least KRW 15 million per year, PhD at least KRW 22 million per year). That is a different funding scheme and is not the subject of this record.
existing.duration: Master's and PhD degree programmes at DGIST; the scholarship page does not state a fixed award duration, and the annual stipend figures are stated per year
existing.application_period: DGIST publishes four intakes per year. For the 2027 academic year: 2027 Spring 1st (online application 26 June to 9 July 2026, closed), 2027 Spring 2nd (27 August to 10 September 2026, closed), 2027 Spring 3rd (5 to 19 November 2026, the next still-applicable window) and 2026 Fall (8 to 22 April 2027).
existing.deadline_display: DGIST 2027 Spring 3rd round online application period: 5 November 2026 to 19 November 2026 (Korean Standard Time)
existing.program_type: University graduate scholarship (government-funded track administered by the university)
